Chapter 3: Building Trust — The Early Days with Tuesday
Those first weeks with Tuesday really felt like a crash course in patience—and in opening up, maybe for the first time in years. Living alongside a service dog, well, it changed everything. Suddenly, life had a new rhythm. There were routines to follow, real responsibilities to handle, and, slowly but surely, a foundation of trust to build.
For someone who’d always tried to keep every feeling locked up tight, letting another being in—even a dog like Tuesday—felt a little strange at first. But you know what? It was also surprisingly comforting.
Every morning began the same way: Tuesday would nudge gently, almost like he was saying, “Hey, I’m here. Let’s get going.” That simple reminder was more powerful than it sounds. Knowing that someone depended on him—feeding, walking, grooming—brought a sense of purpose to days that used to drift by with no direction. Tuesday’s needs were always right there, clear and immediate, and that pulled attention away from all those anxious thoughts spinning in the background.
Heading outside together wasn’t easy. Crowded sidewalks and noisy intersections still made anxiety spike. But Tuesday’s steady presence changed the game. Whenever panic started to bubble up, Tuesday would lean in close, as if to say, “I’ve got you.” His calm was contagious—sometimes, that was all it took to feel grounded again.
Of course, it wasn’t always smooth sailing. There were plenty of setbacks. Some outings just didn’t go well, and on rough days, it was so tempting to just stay inside. But Tuesday? He never got frustrated or pulled away. Instead, he’d stick close, quietly offering support. Over time, those little acts of loyalty began to break down the walls that had been built up by years of pain.
Trusting Tuesday meant letting go of the urge to control every single thing. Back in the Army, control had been everything—a matter of survival. But now, it was just getting in the way of healing. Tuesday’s training was remarkable. He could pick up on anxiety before it even showed, interrupt nightmares, and even fetch medication when things felt overwhelming. That kind of understanding—it was humbling. And, honestly, it was empowering too.
As the days went by, the bond between man and dog just kept growing. Tuesday wasn’t just a helper anymore. He became a confidant, a real source of comfort, and, in a way, a bridge back to the outside world. You’d be surprised how many strangers were drawn to Tuesday’s friendly face—suddenly, conversations popped up that never would’ve happened before. For someone who’d spent so long feeling invisible, those little moments were a reminder that he still had a place in the world.
Most of us don’t realize just how powerful companionship can be. We take comfort and connection for granted—a friend’s presence, a gentle touch. But for anyone living with trauma, those simple things can change everything. Tuesday’s unwavering loyalty showed that, even after all the darkness, hope was still possible. Healing might take time, but with someone by your side—someone who believes in you—it really is possible, one day at a time.
